theme_scores.theme: High, opaque and variable tenant fees
theme_scores.justification: The DCLG market research of 50 agents is described with method ("randomly chose 50 agents... searched their website"), and figures are cross-cited to NALS, ARLA, Generation Rent and Shelter (References 3,4,5,6,10), clearly linking variable/high fees to the claim, though the document never explains why these sources diverge so it stops short of level 3.
The claim rests almost entirely on argument, with only the OFT 2013 market study named in prose with no reference marker or link, so it stays at level 1.

theme_scores.theme: Existing regulation has not fixed the problem
theme_scores.justification: Reference 10 (12% of 912 agents not displaying fees) and Reference 11 (a quarter of NLA-surveyed landlords unaware of tenant fees) are properly cited and directly linked to the claim that transparency rules are not working.

theme_scores.theme: Financial and mobility harm to tenants
theme_scores.justification: Citizens' Advice findings (64% had problems paying, 42% borrowed money) are cited as Reference 13 and directly linked to the harm claim, though the EHS 2014-15 moving-decision stats (35%/34%) appear in this theme without a reference marker.

reasoning: The diagnosis rests on four core themes. 'High, opaque and variable tenant fees' (level 2) is the best evidenced, combining DCLG's own described market research of 50 agents with cited NALS/ARLA/Generation Rent/Shelter figures (References 3-6,10), clearly linking variation and scale of fees to the claim, though the document never assesses why its own cited sources give such different averages (£172 vs £223 vs £400), so it does not reach level 3. 'Principal-agent market failure' (level 1) is mostly reasoned argument; its one evidential anchor, the OFT 2013 market study, is named in prose with no reference number or link. 'Existing regulation has not fixed the problem' (level 2) uses Reference 10 (12% of 912 agents not displaying fees) and Reference 11 (a quarter of NLA landlords unaware of tenant fees), both clearly linked to the enforcement-failure claim. 'Financial and mobility harm to tenants' (level 2) relies on Citizens' Advice data cited as Reference 13 (64% had problems paying, 42% borrowed money), though the EHS moving-decision statistics in the same theme lack a citation marker here. The mean of (2,1,2,2) is 1.75, rounding to 2. The weakest link, and strongest counter-example, is the market-failure theme, which would need a proper citation for the OFT study and some primary data on landlord/agent incentives to reach level 2 itself and push the section toward level 3 overall. To reach level 3 as a whole, the document would need to explicitly weigh the reliability or limitations of its own and third-party fee surveys rather than simply juxtaposing differing figures.
